title: The Spikes Brothers and the Dreamland raid
summary: Williams's band played for the Spikes Brothers at the Dreamland after the Cadillac; a Prohibition raid ended it, and he stayed in Los Angeles until March 1921.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: At that very time. What do you know about that? The Spikes Brothers, did you meet them? Spike Brothers, yeah.

Red Spikes, yeah. Johnny Spikes, yeah. Well, we played at the Dreamland for them. You see, after we left the Cadillac, we went down and played for Spikes. Spike Brothers. And they raided that John and police beat Johnny Spikes, so it was terrible. He was a tenor man. Beat himself in terrible. I never forget that. Yeah? Yes, indeed. What were they raided for?
Prohibition then? Yeah, it was Prohibition.

It was Prohibition then. I guess they must have been selling liquor, you know, imagine, so under the cover, you know. We didn't ever know it. I imagine that's what it was about. Yeah. And I know they closed up the joint. He had a place. The Dreamland Cafe was fourth in Stanford. 
in Los Angeles. And I stayed out to Los Angeles until March the 4th, 1921, from 1919 to 1921.
